meta.about: The set-up flow from the home screen to the briefing, its 3D stage, the new inputs (in play and in the menus), the weapon wheel, the weapon bar and the saved set-up (docs/unreal/LOADOUT.md sections 2, 4 and 7). Strings are in frontend_text.json; the screens name their keys.
meta.units: seconds, degrees, centimetres (Unreal units: this file has no web source)

parity.about: The set-up that must play exactly as the web game (LOADOUT.md 1.2). It is also the set-up of a first start, and what any invalid saved set-up falls back to. Its guns and crew are always offered, ready or not.
parity.fireModes: each gun's fireModes[0] at the start of every run (no fire mode is saved)

carry.note: contiguous: carried guns fill slots 1..n with no gap; removing a gun closes the gap

start.note: the primary button, focused on arrival. Starts at once with the remembered set-up; while save.played is false it opens Crew instead, so every player walks the set-up once. Enter with nothing focused and gamepad Start do the same, as the web title's Enter and Start did

setup.note: the set-up flow from the top

summaryLinks.note: each part of the summary line is a link that opens its screen in edit mode (Next returns to the Briefing)

pickers.note: the web title's three pickers, kept on Home: they write the settings at once, as on the web

screens.note: level card, time, mode and difficulty on one screen; with a second level it splits into level (step 3) and style (step 4)

navigation.about: Shortcuts that keep a returning player fast (LOADOUT.md 2.2).
navigation.edit: a screen opened from a Home summary link or a Briefing Change link is in edit mode: its Next says Done and returns to the Briefing
navigation.stepStrip: a done step can always be clicked; once the set-up is valid every step can be clicked, forward too

toBriefing.note: from any set-up screen, straight to the Briefing when the set-up is valid. Start alone is Next on every set-up screen (Hit the block on Home and the Briefing), so a pad player walks crew, loadout, attachments, block and style in order; the jump is a chord: hold View, press Start

pad: D-pad down past the last row, then A
next.note: the bottom bar's Next takes the focus like any other control: Tab cycles the screen's panes and Next, Down past the last row lands on it

navigation.setupValid: at least one gun carried and every required slot filled (always true after validation)

transitions.about: Every edge of the diagram in LOADOUT.md 2.1. `remember` writes the set-up to the save game when the edge is taken.
edges: first frame of the title state
Hit the block, Enter, gamepad Start, once save.played is true; remember
Hit the block, Enter, Start while save.played is false; Gear up at any time
a link of the summary line (edit mode)
Next (at least one gun carried); remember
Ctrl+Enter or gamepad Start with a valid set-up; Done in edit mode; remember
Change set-up on the death or debrief card (the run ends as Back to title does, then the Briefing opens)

stage.about: The 3D set behind the set-up screens (LOADOUT.md 2.10): a closed room spawned at run time high above the block, so the block's fog, sky light and sun do not reach it. Every value is a placeholder for the art pass.

room.note: a cyclorama room; engine cube walls until the art exists (status missing)

materials.note: world-projected instances of the block's scans (build_block.py TAG_SURFACE / GREY_SURFACE) on the set's engine cubes: a brick back wall behind the gun with two pools of light on it, painted block side walls, a concrete floor, a steel bench top on a dark frame. A missing asset keeps the flat colour (review 2026-11-24: the grey-box stage)

stage.lightsNote: key (front left), fill (front right, on the camera's side: a rect light lights only what is in front of its plane, and the old fill behind the gun drew a hard lit-to-unlit seam across the back wall, fix pass) and a rim from behind right on the gun's top and back edges

bench.note: a steel workbench top under the turntable; status missing

turntable.note: spin: degrees per second when untouched for idleAfter s; drag: degrees per mouse pixel; stick: degrees per second at full right stick; snap: seconds an attachment takes to slide into its socket

arms.eye: the first-person camera of the player rig (spec 02 viewmodel: player.fov.viewmodel 54 degrees)
arms.note: the crew member's arms framed exactly as in play, holding the first carried gun: its Inspect clip, else IdleAds with the rig's sway. Drag orbits up to 10 degrees about the eye; the vignette and a sleeve at the frame edge hide where the arms end, and the closed shoulder caps stay out of view (CHARACTERS.md)

stock.note: the stock slot swaps the base mesh (guns.json variants): the camera frames the stock, the gun is replaced under a 0.15 s dip

focus.note: offsets in centimetres in the gun's frame (X along the bore) from the turntable centre; the camera eases there in 0.4 s when a slot tab is chosen

cameras.title: the title fly-through (spec 04 3.4), kept running behind Home and Block & Style
cameras.firstPerson: the player's own camera at the level's playerStart, the arms holding the first carried gun (Equip, else IdleAds): the intro starts from this view

input.about: Mappings added on top of config.json player.keys / mouseButtons / padButtons (which come from the web game and are not edited). In the parity set-up none of them changes a rule unless pressed.

game.note: replaces the web 'swap' meaning of the wheel and D-pad up: the next carried gun, with config player.input.wheelDebounce (0.28 s) between wheel steps as today. With two guns next = previous = the other gun, which is what swap did
as next, backwards, with the same debounce
unchanged key and, with one or two guns, unchanged behaviour: on press, the other gun. With three or more: the last gun used, on release of a tap; a hold of wheel.hold opens the weapon wheel instead
pad: a tap of View (Back); held for inspectHold it inspects instead

input.magazineCheck: Reload (R, X) with a full magazine, or with an empty reserve, plays the magazine check: the rules refuse the reload as they always did, so nothing else happens

menu.about: Per screen: mouse, keyboard and gamepad. Common to every screen: A, Enter, Space and a left click always activate the focused control; Start, or Enter on the Next button, always advances; Back = B, Esc or the back button (right-click is Back only on screens without a right-click action of their own; on Loadout right-click empties the slot under the cursor and does nothing elsewhere); Ctrl+Enter / Start with a valid set-up jump to the Briefing. In a single-choice row (time, mode, difficulty, Day / Night) moving the focus selects, so A there means Next. The D-pad and left stick move the focus with config player.input.pad.nav (0.6, 0.38 s, 0.17 s).

crew.mouse: click a card to choose; drag the stage to orbit (10 degrees); Next
crew.keys: Left / Right choose (focus selects); Enter next; Esc back
crew.pad: D-pad or stick left / right choose; A or Start next; right stick orbits; B back

loadout.mouse: click a roster card: carry it in the first empty slot, or in the selected slot when all four are full; drag a card onto a slot to put it there; drag a slot onto another to swap their order; right-click a slot to empty it (right-click elsewhere does nothing); the wrench on a card or a slot (or double-click) opens the workbench; drag the stage to turn the gun, wheel zooms
loadout.keys: arrows move the focus over the class tabs, the roster grid and the slots; Enter or Space carries the focused roster gun (or selects the focused slot); 1 to 4 put the focused roster gun in that slot; Shift + Up / Down move the focused slot; Delete empties it; E opens the workbench for the focused gun; Tab jumps between the roster and the slots; Esc back
loadout.pad: D-pad / stick move the focus; A carries the focused roster gun or selects a slot; X empties the focused slot; LB / RB move the focused slot up / down; Y opens the workbench; LT / RT zoom; right stick turns the gun; Start next; B back

workbench.mouse: click a slot tab, then an option; the arrows beside the gun's name (or the carried-gun strip) change gun; hold Reset build for resetHold; drag turns, wheel zooms
workbench.keys: Left / Right slot tab; Up / Down option (previews); Enter or Space fits; Backspace factory part; [ / ] previous / next carried gun; hold R for resetHold to reset the build; Esc done
workbench.pad: D-pad left / right slot tab; up / down option; A fits; X factory part; LB / RB previous / next carried gun; hold Y for resetHold to reset the build; right stick turns; LT / RT zoom; B done

briefing.mouse: Hit the block; Change beside a line opens that screen in edit mode
briefing.keys: Enter hits the block; Up / Down to a Change link, Enter opens it; Esc back
briefing.pad: A or Start hits the block; D-pad to a Change link, A opens it; B back

where.mouse: click a level card; click Day or Night, a mode card, a difficulty; Next
where.keys: Up / Down move between the rows (level, time, mode, difficulty); Left / Right choose in a row (focus selects); Enter next; Esc back
where.pad: D-pad up / down between rows; left / right choose (focus selects); A or Start next; B back

wheel.about: The weapon wheel (LOADOUT.md 4.6). Only with minGuns or more carried; with fewer, Q and Y swap on press exactly as the web game.
wheel.tap: with minGuns or more: a press of Q or Y released before `hold` is a quick swap on release; a hold opens the wheel and starts no swap
wheel.note: deadzone: share of the stick or of mouseRadius (pixels of mouse travel since the wheel opened) below which nothing is selected; releasing there picks nothing. timeScale 1: the game does not slow down

weaponBar.slots: one per carried gun (two in the parity set-up: the web bar exactly), then the melee slot
weaponBar.fireModeTag: AUTO or SEMI under the count of a gun that has both modes
weaponBar.attachmentPips: one small icon per fitted non-baseline attachment, under the gun's silhouette
weaponBar.bag: one reserve count for every finite gun (the shared bag, guns.json ammo), shown once at the right of the bar; each slot shows its own magazine; the NINE shows ∞
weaponBar.inspectPrompt: the T / Hold View prompt shows only for a gun whose Inspect role exists

save.about: The remembered set-up (LOADOUT.md 7), a block of the one save game that also holds the nine settings and the best Hold the Block score (ARCHITECTURE 2.2 Core/Settings/MISaveGame). Mode, difficulty and time stay the existing settings keys and are not copied here.

fields.guns: array of up to 4 names (guns.json ids), slot order
fields.builds: map gun id -> map slot id -> attachment id or None; kept for every gun ever built, carried or not, so a gun put back on keeps its build
fields.seen: array of names: guns, attachments, crew and levels the player has looked at (the NEW badge)
fields.played: bool: at least one run started. While false, Hit the block on Home opens Crew instead of starting

validation: an unknown crew, level or gun id is dropped (a gun pack removed), and so is a gun or crew member that is not offered (not ready): crew -> rule, level -> block, guns -> the remaining ones, and the parity guns when none remains
an attachment not in the gun's compatibility options, or not offered (its mount or variant not exists), is dropped; the slot falls back to its default
a required slot without a valid choice takes its default
duplicates and gaps in guns are removed; more than carry.max are cut
a mode the level does not provide falls back to the first mode it does provide
